# rrffmpeg

> Remote FFmpeg wrapper in Rust. It stands in for `ffmpeg` inside Jellyfin and sends each transcode to the machine that has the GPU, over SSH or through its own agent. Arguments pass through unchanged. It only dispatches: no encoding, remuxing or quality logic.

Update this file in the same change as any doc, config key or feature it lists.
Each entry points at raw Markdown so a reader gets plain text.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/README.md): the pitch, install, the minimal config, and the index of documents.
- [INSTALL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/INSTALL.md): the full install on a client and a worker, the agent daemon, the disk and GPU checks, and the section written for an AI agent.
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/configuration.md): the agent transport, the table that picks a mode, the nine rules for a configured worker, capabilities, and the audit of Jellyfin's `encoding.xml`.
- [Why rrffmpeg exists](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/why.md): the alternatives, the measured defects of rffmpeg, how rrffmpeg answers each one, and the evidence.
- [Status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/status.md): what works in v1, what is next, and the known risks.
- [Operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/operations.md): `rrffmpeg-stats` and how to read the journal report, plus the log levels.
- [Project page](https://vasilvestre.github.io/rrffmpeg/): the same pitch as HTML, plus the current status section.
- [Measured dispatch latency](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/latency.md): how much the dispatcher adds to a transcode start, with the commands to repeat the measurement.
- [rffmpeg against rrffmpeg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/compare-rffmpeg.md): the same job through both dispatchers, on one controlled box and on the production Jellyfin host and its GPU worker, with the breakdown of rffmpeg's cost and the configs to repeat it.
- [Measurer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/scripts/measure.py): 5 warmup runs, N samples, nearest-rank percentiles, used by both benchmark pages.
- [Replay harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/replay.md): records real Jellyfin invocations and replays them through `rrffmpeg` to catch argument, quoting, stream wiring and exit code regressions.
- [Example config](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/config.example.toml): a working pair of client and worker hosts.
- [Release 0.15.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.15.0.md): an absent `concurrency` sizes a worker from its own journal, and the README becomes a pitch plus four documents.
- [Release 0.14.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.14.0.md): pool caps sized from each host's own journal rather than guessed, hysteresis derived from the same tail with no stored counter, and parked jobs (a paused stream) that keep their slot but stop counting toward the cap.
- [Release 0.13.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.13.0.md): Light jobs (probes, thumbnails, trickplay scans) get their own pool and never queue behind a transcode, and a killed dispatcher no longer leaves its local child running or its slot held.
- [Release 0.12.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.12.0.md): a host declares the roots it can read, and placement stops using the order of the `[[hosts]]` blocks.
- [Release 0.11.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.11.0.md): `local = true` puts the client's own GPU in placement, so H.264 stays home and AV1 goes to the worker that can encode it.
- [Release 0.10.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.10.0.md): `rrffmpeg jellyfin` reads Jellyfin's `encoding.xml`, compares each transcode setting with the declared capabilities, and says which hosts can serve it.
- [Release 0.9.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.9.1.md): a host no longer reads as full while slots are free, and the config rejects unknown keys, duplicate host names and zero concurrency.
- [Release 0.9.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.9.0.md): AV1 gets its own capability token per encoder family, so an AV1 job no longer lands on a host that only encodes H.264.
- [Release 0.8.2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.8.2.md): replay no longer moves a writer into another process's block, and a full block is renewed, so journal `seq` values stay unique.
- [Release 0.8.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.8.1.md): journal sequence numbers are reserved per process, so `rrffmpeg-stats` stops reporting phantom open jobs, and orphan events are counted.
- [Release 0.8.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/releases/0.8.0.md): capabilities are sub-tokens proved by one frame per encoder, and `rrffmpeg capabilities` prints the config rows.
- [Install script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/scripts/install.sh): downloads the latest release, checks the checksum, installs the binaries and the `ffmpeg` links, and keeps the previous binary for a rollback.

## Architecture decision records

- [ADR index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/README.md): the table of decisions and their status.
- [0001 Stand in for ffmpeg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0001-stand-in-for-ffmpeg.md): exact argument passthrough.
- [0002 Journal off the critical path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0002-journal-off-the-critical-path.md): append-only journal and background flusher.
- [0003 In-process janitor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0003-in-process-janitor.md): repair in process, no cron watchdog.
- [0004 Prefix path mapping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0004-prefix-path-mapping.md): longest-prefix mapping in both directions.
- [0005 SSH transport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0005-ssh-transport.md): SSH first, behind a trait.
- [0008 Cross-process slots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0008-cross-process-slots.md): slot files and an expiring down verdict.
- [0009 Agent transport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0009-agent-transport.md): the agent daemon as a second transport.
- [0010 Agent TLS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0010-agent-tls.md): one pinned certificate, one connection per direction, amended by 0018.
- [0011 Journal timings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0011-journal-timings.md): timings in the journal, read back by `rrffmpeg-stats`.
- [0012 Shared queue with client weight](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0012-shared-queue-with-client-weight.md): ticket queue orders starts.
- [0013 Retry a job that never started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0013-retry-a-job-that-never-started.md): move an unstarted job to another host.
- [0014 SSH connection persistence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0014-ssh-connection-persistence.md): one long-lived ssh per host, so a job pays a channel open.
- [0015 Journal replay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0015-replay-waits-for-the-janitor.md): the replay runs when the janitor reads it, not at open.
- [0016 Verifiable install and update](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0016-verifiable-install-and-update.md): `--version`, a tag check, one install script, and a protocol revision.
- [0017 The queue decides at the door](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0017-queue-decides-at-the-door.md): a newcomer queues behind a waiter, and free slots are handed out in a batch, measured at 16 concurrent clients.
- [0018 One thread relays a job](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0018-one-thread-relay-and-lazy-stdin.md): the daemon polls both pipes itself, and the stdin connection opens on the first byte.
- [0019 Refuse the local fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0019-refuse-the-local-fallback-for-ffmpeg.md): a transcode fails instead of encoding on a client with no GPU; a probe still falls back.
- [0020 SSH arguments in config](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0020-ssh-arguments-in-config.md): a per-host key without a wrapper script.
- [0021 Per-host environment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0021-per-host-environment.md): the worker wrapper becomes a config table, and the agent protocol moves to revision 2.
- [0022 Progress sample in the journal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0022-progress-sample-in-the-journal.md): fps, speed, source and output shape, and copy or encode per stream, read from the worker's stderr and shipped to Loki.
- [0023 The sample is a peak, not a tail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0023-the-sample-is-a-peak-not-a-tail.md): why the recorded fps and speed are the highest running average, and why the padding ffmpeg puts before a counter hid it.

- [0024 Declared capabilities](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0024-declared-capabilities.md): one token per real driver limit, why libva and ffmpeg cannot answer it, and the one-frame probe that prints the config rows.
- [0025 Reserved sequence numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0025-sequence-numbers-are-reserved-per-process.md): why concurrent processes shared a journal `seq`, and why a block reservation at open fixes identity without touching the record format.
- [0026 Exclusive blocks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0026-a-block-is-exclusive-and-replay-never-moves-the-writer.md): why replaying the journal must not move the writer, and how a full block is renewed.
- [0027 AV1 is a codec token](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0027-av1-is-a-codec-token.md): why an `av1_vaapi` job needed its own token, and why a UHD 630 or an N100 cannot encode AV1.
- [0028 Jellyfin settings audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0028-jellyfin-settings-audit.md): why `rrffmpeg jellyfin` turns each Jellyfin knob into an argument set and reuses the placement rule instead of a second token table.
- [0029 A local host takes part in placement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0029-a-local-host-takes-part-in-placement.md): why `local = true` on a host runs its jobs on the client and lets the scheduler choose between it and a worker.
- [0030 A host declares what it can read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0030-a-host-declares-what-it-can-read.md): why placement skips a host whose declared roots cover no input, and why an empty list keeps the old behaviour.
- [0032 Two pools per host](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0032-two-pools-for-jobs.md): why a probe, a thumbnail and a trickplay scan get their own pool with `light_concurrency`, why a Light job overflows to the local binary instead of waiting, and why the local child is killed with `SIGKILL` when its wrapper dies.
- [0033 Pool caps from measured speed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0033-size-the-pools-from-measured-speed.md): why `concurrency = "auto"` sizes a host from its own journal, how the 5th percentile of solo speeds becomes a cap, why the hysteresis lives in the journal tail instead of a counter file, and why a throttled job is parked instead of counted as slow, amended by 0034.
- [0034 An absent cap is auto everywhere](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0034-an-absent-cap-is-auto-everywhere.md): why an absent `concurrency` is `"auto"` on a remote worker too, since the journal records the speed that worker reported, and why the cost is a cold start at one job.
- [0031 Placement is an order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vasilvestre/rrffmpeg/main/docs/adr/0031-placement-is-an-order-not-the-file.md): the tie-break order that replaces config order, and why a software encode prefers a host that needs no SSH.
